verdict.line: You lose lane if Renekton hits 50+ Fury before you can trade safely, but Shen's 52.6% win rate over 1271 games holds up because he doesn't need to win lane to win the game.

brief.thesis: Renekton has the lane and solo-kill edge because his Reign of Anger passive lets him threaten an empowered, shield-destroying W the moment he banks 50 Fury, and his Q sustains him through your poke on a flat 7s cooldown. Shen's answer isn't to out-trade him in lane, it's to play the defensive shape OP.GG flags: block his real all-in with Feint, poke at range he can't match, and let teleport ult and item spikes convert the matchup on the map instead of at the minion wave.

theirWindow.when: his Fury bar is at or above 50
theirWindow.what: His W (Ruthless Predator) upgrades to a 3-hit slash that destroys damage shields, deals high physical damage, and stuns for 1.5s instead of 0.75s. Don't walk up on him here, and don't pre-shield with Feint expecting it to hold — the empowered version strips it on cast.

yourWindow.when: right after his W or E goes on cooldown
yourWindow.what: W (16-8s CD) and E (16-10s CD) are his only real threats besides autos — once he's used either, step up and poke with Q (475 range), since it outranges his Q (325), W (300), and E (450), and the life tap gets some of that damage straight back to you.

start.why: Measured at 51.5% over 1002 games and the 64.7% pick choice — the flat damage block on his first poke auto and HP5 regen directly counters a lane built around chip autos and Q sustain.

boots.why: 81.4% pick at 53.1% win rate over 1198 games — the physical damage reduction cuts into both his auto-attack Fury generation game and his W/E burst.

core.why: First item on the strongest measured path (56.4% WR, 101 games) — the HP and wave-clear let you survive the 3-10 disadvantage window and start threatening side waves.
Second item on that same path — closes the stat gap that opens once Renekton hits his Fury-fueled power spike.
Caps the 56.4% WR core path and directly punishes an auto-attack-reliant Fury generator with reflected damage.

runes.keystoneWhy: Procs on autos you're already landing in trades, scales HP all game, and is the backbone of the top-picked page (36.6% pick, 53% WR) for exactly this kind of defensive, sustain-through-poke lane.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport posts the best measured win rate (52.7%, 28.4% pick) and matches Shen's actual win condition in this matchup — giving up a close lane to split-push and teleport into fights elsewhere. Flash+Ignite (52.6%, 68.7% pick) is the more common choice if you want to punish any overextension he makes while chasing Fury.

playing.title: Save Feint for his real W
playing.detail: Use W (Feint) to absorb the unempowered two-slash Ruthless Predator, not a guess. If he's already above 50 Fury when he casts it, the upgraded version destroys your shield outright, so you want to bait the first cast while he's still below threshold.

playing.title: Poke with Q, not E
playing.detail: Vorpal Blade's 475 range beats his Q (325), W (300), and E (450), so chip him down from max range and take the lifesteal-style heal instead of closing distance with your own E, which commits you from 575 range into his taunt.

playing.title: Respect a 'low' Renekton
playing.detail: Reign of Anger generates Fury faster the lower his own HP drops, so a Renekton who looks finishable can still have the Fury banked for an empowered W-E combo. Don't force a trade on him without knowing his Fury bar.

playing.title: React, don't initiate
playing.detail: OP.GG's own read on this matchup is to answer his engage rather than start your own. Let him commit E (16-10s CD) into taunt range first, Feint the follow-up, then Q once his gap-closer is spent.

playing.title: Play for the level 11+ item spike
playing.detail: You're behind through the 3-10 window where his Fury and lower W cooldown dominate skirmishes. Prioritize safe farm over contesting trades until Titanic Hydra and Dusk and Dawn come online.

playing.title: Win on the map, not the wave
playing.detail: Stand United's unlimited range and 200-160s cooldown let you trade lane equity for global pressure — ward deep, take skirmishes elsewhere, and use teleport to make his lane lead irrelevant to the final result.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and all win rates/sample sizes above are pulled directly from measured games on the current patch via OP.GG; the tactical reasoning connecting them to specific ability cooldowns and Fury thresholds is our own analysis.

stats.opponentTip: It is important to absorb Renekton’s (W) with [W]. Rather than initiating combat, try to respond to Renekton initiating combat. Be careful when Renekton has his Fury full as it deals a lot of damage!
